name: tiny-unexpected-verification
description: Deduplicated source-review catalog of rounds-1-3 claims, corrected in round 4. Not occurrence counts. Exact matches are excluded; unreviewed is not invalid. Per-round machine-readable verdicts for later rounds are in round4-reviews.json and round5-reviews.json. Full historical trial evidence was not retained, so conditional validity does not validate every original claim.

findings.title: Response cache records no expiry bound for tokens lacking iat, so expired tokens keep verifying until cacheTTL elapses
findings.note: Reproduced with signed HS256 exp token lacking iat: cache:true accepts it after expiry; uncached and numeric-iat controls reject. Same root cause at both lines. Meaningful expiry bypass, cache opt-in required. See round4-jwt-verification.json.

findings.title: Cached verification ignores a token's exp whenever the payload has no numeric iat
findings.note: Reproduced with signed HS256 exp token lacking iat: cache:true accepts it after expiry; uncached and numeric-iat controls reject. Same root cause at both lines. Meaningful expiry bypass, cache opt-in required. See round4-jwt-verification.json.

findings.title: Signature verification skipped for tokens with an empty signature segment when no key material is resolved
findings.note: Original none/no-key rationale is intended opt-in, not a vulnerability. A different HS256/null-key configuration does accept an empty HS256 signature (reproduced). Async null-key results are rejected. Full original evidence is unavailable; do not infer which claim was made from its sink alone. Dataset now separates intended none control from signed-algorithm null-key failure.

findings.title: Tokens with an empty signature are accepted when the configured key is empty/null
findings.note: Original none/no-key rationale is intended opt-in, not a vulnerability. A different HS256/null-key configuration does accept an empty HS256 signature (reproduced). Async null-key results are rejected. Full original evidence is unavailable; do not infer which claim was made from its sink alone. Dataset now separates intended none control from signed-algorithm null-key failure.

findings.title: O_TRUNC is applied before flock ownership, so a losing contender truncates the holder's lock file
findings.note: Truncating an ordinary lock file before flock is not automatically the expected symlink-target violation. Need original evidence of a meaningful protected-data consequence, not shared line/CWE overlap.

findings.title: UnixFileLock follows a symlink at the lock path and truncates its target (no O_NOFOLLOW/O_EXCL)
findings.note: The os.open call that follows the symlink; same root cause one line later.

findings.title: raise_on_not_writable_file uses os.stat, following a symlink at the lock path
findings.note: os.stat at line 22 only reads metadata and gates an error. Following the symlink here alone neither truncates nor changes permissions; the actual unsafe mutation is os.open in _unix.py. No distinct security violation was established.

findings.title: WindowsFileLock opens the lock path with O_CREAT|O_TRUNC following redirects
findings.note: Historical broad blind instruction differs from Unix-only labeled case. Windows reparse-point exploit was not reproduced here; do not count as verified valid merely by matching a title or assume out-of-scope under the blind instruction.

findings.title: Chunked-body footer consumed without CRLF validation (HTTP request smuggling)
findings.note: The _bytes_to_discard branch that consumes the unvalidated footer; same bug as line 197.

findings.title: ChunkedReader accepts arbitrary bytes as the chunk footer, enabling HTTP request smuggling
findings.note: This is the manifest exact key and must never enter unexpected metrics.

findings.title: lock()/unlock() pass unvalidated key and nonce sizes to crypto_aead_lock/unlock (out-of-bounds read)
findings.note: crypto_aead_lock receives unvalidated key/nonce sizes (documented 32/24) without checks.

findings.title: chacha20() validates the nonce length but not the key length (out-of-bounds read)
findings.note: chacha20 validates the nonce length but not the key length.

findings.title: Unbounded BLAKE2b key length overflows fixed stack buffer in keyed init
findings.note: Genuine: blake2b passes unbounded len(key) to crypto_blake2b_keyed, which COPYs into u8 key_block[128].

findings.title: argon2i_32 ignores NULL from malloc and does not bound nb_blocks
findings.note: Missing malloc NULL check at wrapper line 345 is a separate failure path from too-small nb_blocks. Native crypto_argon2 dereferences the work area; real allocation failure is required. Source-verified, not a reproduced OOM crash.

findings.title: Unvalidated nb_blocks plus unchecked malloc overrun or NULL-deref the Argon2 work area
findings.note: Expected line 345, heap-overflow CWE instead of CWE-122.

findings.title: signature_check trusts fixed-size buffers, allowing out-of-bounds read of untrusted input
findings.note: signature_check passes fixed-size expectations without validating buffer lengths.

findings.title: ThinVec::clear drops elements before resetting len, causing double-free if an element destructor panics
findings.note: ThinVec::clear has the same panic-unwind double-drop; the 0.2.16 fix patches it too.

findings.title: gecko-ffi reallocate loses the length when moving an auto array to the heap
findings.note: gecko-ffi header loses length when moving an auto array; fix adds set_len. Feature-specific leak/correctness issue; medium-or-higher security impact has not been demonstrated.

findings.title: IntoIter::drop double-drops the buffer if a destructor panics, because the temporary ThinVec keeps its original len
findings.note: The drop_in_place call in the same IntoIter::drop bug.

findings.title: Block index underflow lets a prover force the SHA256 output to zero (unsound hash)
findings.note: The out-of-range selector index in Sha256General; same bug as the LessEqThan sink.
